title: ticfac-run-state.json: say that attempt numbers are run-wide identity, not a per-tick count
description:
The contract's prose around attempt numbering reads as though each tick counts its own attempts from 1. The code treats the number as RUN-WIDE identity — attempt 27 is the 27th attempt of the run, whichever tick it belongs to — and the per-tick count is a separate notion (the 'try').

Two readers have now had to derive this from the code rather than the contract. It has already produced a real bug: a ticfac test hardcoded run-wide numbers as if they were per-tick and broke when the dispatch window let two ticks interleave (fixed with markerTierOfTry).

Work: state the distinction in the contract, name both quantities, and make the golden cases carry an example where they differ — a golden where attempt and try coincide documents nothing.

Reported by ticfac run epic-ncv, tick z23, finding 829f846d.
acceptance_criteria: The contract names attempt (run-wide) and try (per-tick) distinctly, and at least one golden case has attempt != try
